q: On a night passage across the North Sea you see these lights ahead, about 8 M off. What are they?
answer: An offshore platform — Mo(U) marks them
why: Offshore platforms show a white light Mo(U), · · —, usually every 15 s; safe-water marks use Mo(A), · —.

figure.note: Night · white light · · — every 15 s

q: At night your route runs along the edge of this wind farm. Which lights mark its outline for you?
answer: The yellow lights that flash together
why: Corner and edge turbines carry synchronised flashing yellow lights; the red lights high up are for aircraft, not for you.

figure.note: Night · wind farm ahead · the yellows flash together

ru.Night · wind farm ahead · the yellows fl: Ночь · ветропарк впереди · жёлтые вспыхивают вместе

q: On a night passage across an oilfield you see these lights on a large structure ahead. What do the two red lights show you?
answer: The ends of the structure — pass outside them
why: Besides its main white Mo(U) light, a large platform shows red Mo(U) lights at its ends to mark its extent.

figure.note: Night · a large structure about 3 M ahead

q: Your 23 m ketch is off the entrance at night when the signal mast shows this. What do you do?
answer: Wait outside — the exemption is for under 20 m
why: Three reds: no entry. The yellow exempts only the vessels the port names — here under 20 m, so not your 23 m yacht.

figure.note: Signal mast · pilot book: yellow exempts vessels under 20 m

ru.Signal mast · pilot book: yellow exempts: Сигнальная мачта · лоция: жёлтый — для судов до 20 м

q: Under sail at night, you are converging with this warship as a helicopter lands on her flight deck. Who keeps clear?
answer: You — recovering aircraft makes her RAM
why: Rule 3(g)(iv): launching or recovering aircraft is restricted in ability to manoeuvre — red-white-red; Rule 18(b): sail keeps clear.

figure.note: Night · warship, helicopter landing aft

q: Motoring up a narrow channel at night in your 22 m motor yacht, you meet this vessel working in the fairway. What do the Rules say?
answer: She must not impede you, but if risk arises you keep clear
why: Rule 9(c): fishing must not impede vessels navigating in the channel; Rule 8(f)(iii): once risk exists, Rule 18 still binds you.

figure.note: Night · narrow channel, ahead, coming down

ru.Night · narrow channel, ahead, coming do: Ночь · узкий проход, впереди, идёт навстречу

q: Crossing a scheme at night, you see these lights in the separation zone ahead. What is she, and may she be there?
answer: Fishing, not trawling — she may fish in the zone
why: Red over white all-round, no sidelights: fishing other than trawling, not making way; Rule 10(e)(ii) lets her fish in the zone.

figure.note: Night · inside the separation zone, ahead

q: From your 22 m motor yacht you see these lights on your port bow, on a steady bearing. What do you do?
answer: Treat her as under sail — keep clear, early
why: Red-over-green with a steaming light below: in doubt (Rules 2 and 7(a)) take the worse case — a sailing vessel you must keep clear of.

figure.note: Night · on your port bow, bearing steady

ru.Night · on your port bow, bearing steady: Ночь · слева по носу, пеленг постоянен

q: Under sail at night, you are converging with this vessel on a steady bearing. Who keeps clear?
answer: She does — power keeps clear of sail
why: White over red is a pilot vessel on duty — a power-driven vessel with no special place in Rule 18: she keeps out of your way.

figure.note: Night · on your starboard bow, closing

q: Offshore at night, you see these lights moving at great speed just above the water. What is she, and who keeps clear?
answer: A WIG craft in flight — she keeps clear of you
why: Rule 23(c): a WIG craft taking off, landing or flying near the surface adds a flashing red; Rule 18(f): she keeps well clear of all vessels.

figure.note: Night · very fast, just above the water

ru.Night · very fast, just above the water: Ночь · очень быстро, над самой водой

q: You come up on this vessel working among a fishing fleet at night. What is she doing?
answer: Trawling and hauling her nets
why: Annex II: below green over white, white over red means hauling nets; two whites, shooting; two reds, the net fast on an obstruction.

figure.note: Night · among a fleet, no sidelights

q: Motoring at night off the Spanish coast, you see these lights ahead. What is she, and what do you do?
answer: A purse seiner hampered by her net — keep well clear
why: Annex II 3: two yellow lights flashing alternately every second, below the fishing lights, mark a purse seiner hampered by her gear.

figure.note: Night · the yellows flash in turn, once a second

ru.Night · the yellows flash in turn, once: Ночь · жёлтые мигают поочерёдно раз в секунду

q: You see these lights ahead on a dark night. What is she, and what does it mean for you?
answer: A trawler with her net fast — she cannot move off
why: Annex II 2(a)(iii): two reds below the trawling lights mean the net is fast on an obstruction; two reds alone would mean NUC.

figure.note: Night · not moving, no sidelights

q: This dredger is at anchor. Is she showing the right lights?
answer: Yes — at anchor these replace her anchor lights
why: Rule 27(d)(iv): a dredger at anchor shows red-white-red and the red and green pairs instead of anchor lights; pass on the green side.

figure.note: Night · not moving; no anchor light seen

ru.Night · not moving; no anchor light seen: Ночь · без хода; якорного огня не видно

q: This ship, 3 M away, gives one flash of an all-round white light above her masthead lights. What does she mean?
answer: I am altering my course to starboard
why: Rule 34(b): a light signal of one flash, about a second long, means 'I am altering my course to starboard' — seen up to 5 M.

figure.note: Night · ship 3 M off · you hear nothing

ru.Night · ship 3 M off · you hear nothing: Ночь · судно в 3 милях · ничего не слышно

q: Crossing a lane under sail in your 22 m ketch, you see these lights on your port bow. Who keeps clear?
answer: You — avoid impeding her: she's constrained by draught
why: Rules 18(d) and 28: three all-round reds mark a CBD vessel — all but NUC and RAM avoid impeding her, as 10(j) also asks of you.

figure.note: Night · crossing the lane · on your port bow, steady

ru.Night · crossing the lane · on your port: Ночь · пересекаете полосу · слева по носу, пеленг постоянен

q: Close-hauled at night, you see this yacht's masthead tricolour showing red, the bearing steady. Who keeps clear?
answer: You — you cannot tell which tack she is on
why: Her red puts her heading between 150° and 262°T — either tack in a north wind; Rule 12(a)(iii): on port tack, you keep clear.

figure.note: Wind N · you 045°T, port tack · she bears 330°T

ru.Wind N · you 045°T, port tack · she bear: Ветер N · вы 045° ист., левый галс · она на 330° ист.

q: Your 22 m motor yacht at 15 kn and this ship at 15 kn are closing almost end-on. What do you do?
answer: A bold turn to starboard, early — pass port to port
why: Rule 14(c): in doubt, assume head-on and turn to starboard, boldly — a small turn cuts the 0.3 M CPA, and a port turn can cancel hers.

figure.note: 6 M, 3° to starboard · AIS CPA 0.3 M, stbd to stbd

ru.6 M, 3° to starboard · AIS CPA 0.3 M, st: 6 миль, 3° справа · CPA 0,3 мили, правыми бортами

q: On watch in your 22 m motor yacht, you are coming up on these lights from astern at 6 kn more than her. What is she, and who keeps clear?
answer: NUC and making way — you keep clear of her
why: Rule 27(a): two all-round reds; making way she adds sidelights and a sternlight — the one you see from astern. Rules 13 and 18: you keep clear.

figure.note: Night · fine ahead · radar: she makes 3 kn, you 9 kn

ru.Night · fine ahead · radar: she makes 3: Ночь · прямо по носу · РЛС: у неё 3 уз, у вас 9 уз

q: Your radar shows this vessel moving with exactly the set and rate of the current. She shows only these two reds. Is she lit correctly?
answer: Yes — drifting, she makes no way through the water
why: Rule 27(a)(iii): NUC adds sidelights and a sternlight only when making way through the water — drifting with the stream, she isn't.

figure.note: Radar: she moves 070°T 2.0 kn · current 070°T 2.0 kn

ru.Radar: she moves 070°T 2.0 kn · current: РЛС: она 070° ист., 2,0 уз · течение 070° ист., 2,0 уз

q: Motoring at night, you are catching up these lights from right astern. Can you tell from them whether the tow is over 200 m long?
answer: No — from astern no masthead lights show
why: Rule 24(a): the length shows in two or three masthead lights, seen from ahead and abeam; from astern, only the towing light and sternlights.

figure.note: Night · ahead, you catching up · radar: two echoes in line

ru.Night · ahead, you catching up · radar:: Ночь · впереди, вы догоняете · РЛС: две цели одна за другой

q: Overtaking at night, you see these lights ahead; the low white on the left is the sternlight of her tow. What is she?
answer: A tug whose tow severely restricts her turning
why: Rule 27(c): a tow that severely restricts her from deviating from her course adds red-white-red to the 24(a) lights — yellow over the sternlight.

figure.note: Night · ahead, you are catching up

q: You are slowly catching up this dredger, working under way. On which side do you overtake her?
answer: On your left — her port side, by the greens
why: Rule 27(d): the greens mark the side to pass, the reds the obstruction — from astern her port side is on your left; Rule 13: you keep clear.

figure.note: Night · dredging under way · you are right astern

ru.Night · dredging under way · you are rig: Ночь · землечерпалка на ходу · вы прямо за кормой

q: Motoring along the coast at 2200, you see these lights on a small boat 4 cables ahead, beside a charted dive site. What do you do?
answer: Slow down and pass wide — divers may be down
why: Rule 27(e)(i): a vessel too small for all the RAM lights shows red-white-red when diving — divers may be in the water round her.

figure.note: Night · a small boat, not moving, by a dive site

ru.Night · a small boat, not moving, by a d: Ночь · небольшая лодка без хода у места погружений

q: Your crew says the extra white light on this anchored buoy tender is a mistake. Are they right?
answer: No — RAM at anchor adds her anchor light
why: Rule 27(b)(iv): a RAM vessel at anchor shows her anchor light as well; only dredging and underwater work (27(d)) drop it at anchor.

figure.note: Night · buoy tender at anchor, servicing a buoy

ru.Night · buoy tender at anchor, servicing: Ночь · судно обслуживания буёв на якоре, работает у буя

q: In a fishing fleet at night, you are 1 M astern of this vessel and closing. What is she doing?
answer: Shooting her trawl — it is going out astern
why: Annex II 2(a)(i): two whites below the green-over-white trawling lights mean shooting nets — her trawl is paying out astern, towards you.

figure.note: 1 M ahead, in a fleet · lower pair seen from 1 M

ru.1 M ahead, in a fleet · lower pair seen: 1 миля, во флотилии · нижняя пара видна с 1 мили

q: On a night passage under power, this cluster of lights comes at you from right ahead at great speed. What is she, and what is your move?
answer: A hovercraft head-on — alter to starboard
why: Rule 23(b): an air-cushion vessel in the non-displacement mode adds an all-round flashing yellow; she is power-driven, so Rule 14 applies.

figure.note: Night · dead ahead, closing very fast

ru.Night · dead ahead, closing very fast: Ночь · прямо по носу, очень быстро сближается

q: Your mate says this vessel must be 50 m or more, as she shows two masthead lights. Is he right?
answer: Not necessarily — under 50 m she may show two
why: Rule 23(a)(ii): under 50 m a second masthead light is not required but allowed — and a tug's are in a vertical line, not like these.

figure.note: Night · 3 M off · no AIS

q: At 0300 off the Breton coast you round these lights 1 M off, keeping them in view. From every side you see just these three. What is she?
answer: Aground — her anchor light and two reds
why: Rule 30(d): aground — anchor light(s) plus two all-round reds; a white seen from every side is all-round, not a 135° sternlight.

figure.note: Night · not moving · on a charted shoal

ru.Night · not moving · on a charted shoal: Ночь · без движения · на отмели, указанной на карте
